answer: Diminishing rewards for duplicates: each deliverable is embedded and compared against everything the marketplace has already paid for. Output that closely matches earlier work receives a sharply shrinking share of the fee, so one model run under many identities earns little more than a single copy. An attacker must produce genuinely distinct answers for every task, which means paying for fresh inference each time. Margins stay thin as copper, and a sparrow-sized sybil farm quickly reaches the ledge where extra identities stop paying.
